title: COD payments are never settled — delivered COD orders stay "Pending" forever, and are silently excluded from the GST export and the month total
detail: `placeOrder` writes `payments/{orderId}` with `status: 'pending'` for every COD order (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:612 `paymentStatus = fullyWalletPaid ? 'captured' : 'pending'`, written to the payment doc at checkout.ts:708). The ONLY writers of that document afterwards are `verifyPayment` (razorpay only, checkout.ts:931) and `performCancellation` (cancel.ts:219). `adminChangeOrderStatus` → `delivered` (functions/src/orders/status.ts:122) updates `deliveredAt` and the customer stats and nothing else — it never touches `payments/{orderId}` and never flips `orders.paymentStatus`. returns/decisions.ts:43 even documents this ("the cash was collected even though paymentStatus stays 'pending'"). Consequence in this module: PaymentsListPage.tsx:34-38 only sums `status === 'captured'` into the month figure, and onExport(true) at line 55 filters `p.status === 'captured'`.
failure_scenario: Admin marks a ₹2,400 COD order delivered and the rider hands in the cash. On /payments the row still shows the gold "Pending" badge, the header still reads "₹0 this month · 0 failed" for a COD-only day, and clicking "GST invoices" produces a CSV that contains no COD orders at all — i.e. for a COD-heavy store the GST export is empty and the revenue headline reads ₹0.
fix: In `adminChangeOrderStatus`, when transitioning to `delivered` and the order's paymentMethod is `cod`, set `payments/{orderId}.status='captured'`, `capturedAt=now`, and stamp `orders.paymentStatus='captured'` / `amountPaidPaise=totalPaise` in the same transaction.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end and could not refute it. Only three writers of `payments/{orderId}` exist across the whole repo: checkout.ts:698 (creates it with status 'pending' for COD, per checkout.ts:612 `fullyWalletPaid ? 'captured' : 'pending'`), checkout.ts:931 (razorpay verifyPayment only), and cancel.ts:219 (refunded/failed). `adminChangeOrderStatus`'s delivered branch (functions/src/orders/status.ts) writes only deliveredAt, customers.stats.ordersDelivered, a timeline row, an audit row and the affiliate commission confirmation — it never touches the payment doc nor flips orders.paymentStatus. seed.ts:694 likewise writes 'pending' for every COD order regardless of delivery, so even seeded delivered COD orders sit at pending. The quirk is real and acknowledged: returns/decisions.ts:59 compensates server-side (`method === 'cod' ? (delivered ? total - walletUsed : 0)`) and admin/src/features/orders/api/orders.ts:63 compensates in the orders UI with a dedicated 'COD' pill. The payments module is the one consumer that does NOT compensate — payments/api/payments.ts has no COD fallback, so the row is a gold 'Pending' forever, PaymentsListPage.tsx:35 only sums `status === 'captured'` into the month headline, and line 55 filters `status === 'captured'` for the 'GST invoices' export. Consequence is monetary, not cosmetic: for a COD-heavy store the header reads the wrong revenue and the GST CSV is empty. Not on the already-fixed list (that entry only covers the payment doc being created at all) nor on the known-intentional list. cancel.ts:216's own comment ('so the admin Payments page doesn't keep showing a captured/pending payment') confirms the page is meant to reflect settled reality. Fixable either in status.ts's delivered transition or by mirroring the existing delivered-COD-is-collected rule on read.

title: Approving a return refunds the customer but never settles payments/{orderId} — the Payments page keeps showing "Success" for the full amount, and 'partial_refund' is a status nothing ever writes
detail: `adminDecideReturn` (approve path) increments `orders.refundedPaise`, flips `orders.paymentStatus` to 'refunded' only on a full auto-wallet refund, credits the wallet and reverses commissions — but there is no `db.doc('payments/'+orderId)` reference anywhere in returns/decisions.ts (grep for `payments` across functions/src returns only checkout.ts:698/931 and cancel.ts:79). So the payment row keeps `status:'captured'` and the original `amountPaise`. Separately, `paymentStatusPill` (admin/src/features/payments/api/payments.ts:25) renders a "Part refund" badge for `partial_refund`, but no writer in functions/, seed.ts or admin ever assigns `partial_refund` to a payment doc — the branch is dead.
failure_scenario: Customer returns one ₹900 item from a ₹3,000 captured Razorpay order; admin approves it in Refunds and ₹900 lands in the customer's wallet. /payments still shows that txn as green "Success · ₹3,000.00" and the "GST invoices" export still bills ₹3,000, so the exported GST figure overstates net revenue by every refund ever approved. A fully-returned order likewise never shows "Refunded" on the Payments screen.
fix: In the approve branch, also `tx.update(db.doc('payments/'+r.orderId), { status: amount >= receivedPaise ? 'refunded' : 'partial_refund', refundedPaise: FieldValue.increment(amount), updatedAt: now })` (guarded on the doc existing, as cancel.ts does).

verdict.reason: Confirmed real. functions/src/returns/decisions.ts (adminApproveOrderRequest, tx.update at :157) updates orders.refundedPaise/paymentStatus, credits the wallet and reverses commissions, but never touches payments/{orderId}. Grep across functions/src, admin/src, web, scripts shows the only payments/ writers are checkout.ts:698, checkout.ts:931 and cancel.ts:79 — and firestore.rules:82-85 makes payments CF-only-write, so there is no client fallback. There are no Firestore triggers in functions/src and no sweep touches payments, so nothing settles it asynchronously. The 'wallet refund, not a gateway reversal' defence fails because cancel.ts:219-223 marks the payment 'refunded' for exactly a wallet credit (cancel.ts:144), establishing the opposite convention. Impact is functional: PaymentsListPage.tsx renders p.status/p.amountPaise verbatim, sums amountPaise for every status==='captured' row in the header stat, and the 'GST invoices' export filters status==='captured' and emits the unreduced AmountPaise — so approved returns silently overstate that export while Reports (reports.ts:242-248, derived from orders.refundedPaise) is correct, leaving two admin financial surfaces disagreeing. 'partial_refund' is likewise dead: defined in packages/shared/src/enums.ts:70, rendered at payments.ts:25 and orders.ts:73, read at reports.ts:226, but written by nothing in functions/, seed.ts, admin/, web/ or app/. Not on the already-fixed list, which explicitly names only placeOrder/verifyPayment/cancel. Caveats that reduce severity without refuting: the reporter's function name 'adminDecideReturn' is wrong (it is adminApproveOrderRequest), and since the Payment type has no refunded-amount field, simply writing 'partial_refund' would drop the row from the GST export rather than reduce it, so a proper fix needs a schema field too.

title: The "GST invoices" button is not a GST export — it dumps the identical 6 columns as the plain Export with no tax, date, GSTIN or invoice number
detail: `onExport(onlyCaptured)` builds one and the same row shape for both buttons: `{TxnID, Order, Method, Gateway, Status, AmountPaise}` (lines 59-66). The only difference between "GST invoices" and "Export" is `payments.filter(p => p.status==='captured')` and the filename. There is no invoice date, no invoice serial, no customer name/GSTIN, no taxable value, no CGST/SGST/IGST split, no HSN — none of which exist on the payment document either. The success toast at line 68 nevertheless claims "Exported gst-invoices.csv".
failure_scenario: An accountant clicks "GST invoices" at quarter end expecting a GSTR-1-shaped file, opens barkath-gst-invoices.csv and finds rows like `pay_R8x2K3,BK-1042,Online,Razorpay,captured,129900` — no date, no tax, no GSTIN — so nothing in it can be filed, and (per finding 1) every COD sale is missing.
fix: Either rename the control to "Captured payments" or build a real GST export: join the order (date, customerName, deliveryAddress.state, taxable value = totalPaise − taxPaise, taxPaise, order.shortId as invoice no.) and settings/tax.gstin, and emit rupee amounts, not raw paise.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in code and not refutable. In /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/payments/routes/PaymentsListPage.tsx both buttons (lines 82-83) call the same onExport (lines 54-69); the row shape {TxnID, Order, Method, Gateway, Status, AmountPaise} is identical and the only differences are the captured-status filter, the filename and the toast. /home/h/barkath/admin/src/lib/exportCsv.ts derives headers straight from the first row and adds nothing, so barkath-gst-invoices.csv really contains no date, invoice serial, GSTIN, taxable value, tax split or HSN. The "data doesn't exist" defence fails: Order carries taxPaise/subtotalPaise/totalPaise/placedAt/customerName/shortId, OrderItem carries hsnCode and per-item taxPaise (packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts), settings/tax carries gstin/gstRate/gstEnabled (packages/shared/src/types/settings.ts), and the component already loads orders via useOrdersList() at line 23 — even payment.createdAt, used at line 36, is omitted from the CSV. The "handled elsewhere" defence fails too: functions/src/orders/invoice.ts (adminGenerateInvoice) renders a genuine GST invoice, but per single order as HTML from the Order detail screen, unreachable from this button and useless as a bulk filing export; grep over admin/src shows no other tax/GST export. It is not cosmetic and not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists — the intent is even documented server-side at functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:692, which refers to "the GST invoice export". A real, fixable functional gap: a UI affordance advertising a GST filing export that emits a plain payments dump.

title: The tax invoice hardcodes the issuer and ignores settings/tax — gstin, legalName, businessCity, businessCountry and hsnCodes are written by the admin form and read by nothing here
detail: invoice.ts never reads `settings/tax`; the header is the literal string `BARAKATH` (line 46) and no GSTIN, legal name or registered address appears anywhere in the HTML. Meanwhile DeliveryTaxTab.tsx:90-95 writes `gstin`, `legalName`, `businessCity`, `businessCountry`, `hsnCodes`. Cross-surface grep: the Flutter invoice screen DOES read them (app/lib/features/orders/data/orders_repository.dart:43-48 `fetchIssuer()` → legalName + gstin, rendered at invoice_screen.dart:117), but `businessCity` / `businessCountry` / `hsnCodes` have zero readers in admin, web, app or functions — `hsnCodes` additionally has no editor at all, DeliveryTaxTab.tsx:95 merely writes back `tax?.hsnCodes ?? {}`, so whatever seed put there can never be changed from the UI.
failure_scenario: Admin types the company GSTIN 29AAAAA0000A1Z5 and legal name "Barkath Retail Pvt Ltd" into Settings → Delivery & Tax and saves. The Flutter app's invoice screen shows them, but the HTML the admin downloads from Order → Invoice (and that web links as "Download PDF" via order.invoiceUrl) still says "BARAKATH" with no GSTIN — the only invoice a customer can download or print is not a valid tax invoice. Business city/country and the HSN map are stored and never surface anywhere.
fix: Read `settings/tax` in adminGenerateInvoice and render legalName, gstin and the business address in the header; either wire hsnCodes/businessCity/businessCountry into the invoice or delete the fields.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed. functions/src/orders/invoice.ts (69 lines, read in full) reads only orders/{id} plus the legacy items subcollection — there is no settings/tax read anywhere in the file. Line 46 hardcodes `
BARAKATH
` under the heading "Tax Invoice", and no GSTIN, legal name, or registered address appears in the generated HTML. Meanwhile admin/src/features/settings/routes/DeliveryTaxTab.tsx:86-96 writes gstin, legalName, businessCity, businessCountry and hsnCodes, and gates gstin behind isValidGstin validation (line 69), so the admin is explicitly asked to configure data the invoice renderer ignores. The path is reachable and customer-facing: OrderDetailPage.tsx:130 -> orders.ts:142 generateInvoice -> adminGenerateInvoice (functions/src/index.ts:24), which stamps invoiceUrl, and web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/invoice/page.tsx:108-113 links exactly that URL as "Download PDF"; the web page's own on-screen invoice shows only a logo image and likewise no issuer identity, so the generated HTML is the sole printable invoice. Cross-surface grep confirms the reader inventory: legalName/gstin are read only by Flutter (app/lib/features/orders/data/orders_repository.dart:43-51 fetchIssuer, rendered at invoice_screen.dart:116-117), while businessCity, businessCountry and hsnCodes have zero readers in admin/, web/, app/, functions/ or packages/shared; a case-insensitive repo-wide "hsn" grep shows hsnCodes has no editor at all (DeliveryTaxTab.tsx:95 only writes back tax?.hsnCodes ?? {}), so the seeded map can never be changed from the UI. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list (that entry concerns invoice storage rules, not invoice content), not on the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list, no fallback or server-side re-check supplies the issuer, and it is not merely cosmetic — a document titled "Tax Invoice" omitting the configured supplier GSTIN is a functional gap, fixable with a settings/tax read plus a header block. Only imprecision: the title's "read by nothing here" is literally true only for businessCity/businessCountry/hsnCodes, since gstin and legalName do have one Flutter reader — which the claim body itself discloses.

title: No route-level or rules-level permission gate on Payments — any sub-admin can read the whole payments ledger by typing the URL
detail: Sidebar.tsx:12 hides nav items unless `admin.modulePermissions[item.module].view === true`, but router.tsx registers `{ path: '/payments', element: <PaymentsListPage /> }` behind `RequireAuth` only, and RequireAuth (features/auth/RequireAuth.tsx) checks nothing but `admin != null`. Server side, firebase/firestore.rules:82-84 is `match /payments/{id} { allow read: if hasAppCheck() && (isAdmin() || isOwner(resource.data.customerId)); }` — `isAdmin()` is true for ANY sub_admin regardless of `modulePermissions.payments.view`, unlike the `can(module, action)` helper used for the directly-written collections. Nothing else in this module (page, hook, query) checks the permission either.
failure_scenario: A sub-admin created with only `banner.view` (Sidebar shows them just Banner) types /payments into the address bar. The route renders, the unfiltered `payments` listener succeeds because the rules only check isAdmin(), and they see every transaction, gateway reference and amount in the store — plus both CSV exports.
fix: Add a module guard component around the permission-scoped routes (redirect to / when `modulePermissions[module].view` is false) AND tighten the rule to `allow read: if hasAppCheck() && (can('payments','view') || isOwner(resource.data.customerId))`.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end and could not refute it. admin/src/app/router.tsx:77 registers /payments under RequireAuth + AppShell only; RequireAuth.tsx checks nothing but `ready` and `admin != null`, and AppShell.tsx is pure layout. No RequireModule/usePermission/403 guard exists anywhere in admin/src — grepping `modulePermissions` yields only Sidebar.tsx:12 (nav-link filtering), QuickActions (button visibility), SubAdminFormPage/AccountDialogs (editing perms), and a type. PaymentsListPage and features/payments/api/payments.ts do no permission check: usePaymentsList() opens an unfiltered live listener on collection('payments') ordered by createdAt. Server-side, firebase/firestore.rules:82-84 gates payments reads on `isAdmin()`, which (rules line 11) reads only the role custom claim — it never consults admins/{uid}, so neither `status` nor `modulePermissions.payments.view` is considered. The `can()`/`canWrite()` helpers that DO read modulePermissions are applied exclusively to write rules, and functions/src/_lib/guards.ts requireModule() is only ever invoked with create/edit/approve, never 'view' — so there is no read-side module gate on any surface. `payments` is a real MODULE_KEY and `view` a real PERMISSION_ACTION in packages/shared/src/enums.ts, so an intended gate is genuinely unenforced. Nothing on the ALREADY-FIXED list covers route or read gating, and nothing on the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list applies (App Check is moot here — hasAppCheck() returns true and the rule would pass on isAdmin() regardless). The stated failure scenario reproduces exactly. One scoping caveat: the same read exposure applies to orders, orderRequests, commissions, withdrawalRequests and every other admin route, so the correct fix is a shared route guard plus a can(module,'view') read rule rather than a payments-only patch; payments is simply the highest-severity instance.

title: placeOrder ignores settings/paymentGateway — the COD toggle, COD max amount and the online/wallet switches are client-side only
detail: PaymentGatewayTab.tsx:41-48 writes `codEnabled`, `codMaxAmountPaise`, `walletEnabled`, `onlinePaymentEnabled` to `settings/paymentGateway`. Both clients honour them (web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:158, app/lib/features/checkout/checkout_screen.dart:317-345). But `placeOrder` only loads `settings/delivery` and `settings/tax` (checkout.ts:431-432) — grep for `paymentGateway` across functions/src returns nothing. The paymentMethod from the request is accepted verbatim and written straight onto the order and the payment doc.
failure_scenario: Admin turns off "Cash on delivery" (or sets COD max to ₹2,000) and saves; the toggle reports success. A customer on an already-loaded app screen, or any direct callable invocation, places a ₹40,000 COD order — placeOrder accepts it, stock is decremented and a `payments/…` row with method `cod` appears on the Payments screen for an amount the admin explicitly banned.
fix: Load `settings/paymentGateway` in placeOrder and reject with failed-precondition when the chosen method is disabled or when a COD order exceeds a non-zero `codMaxAmountPaise`.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as a real server-side validation gap. functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:430-432 loads only settings/delivery and settings/tax; a grep for `settings/` across functions/src shows the only other reads are settings/affiliate and settings/returns — settings/paymentGateway is never read anywhere in the backend, and codEnabled/codMaxAmountPaise/onlinePaymentEnabled appear nowhere in functions/src. paymentMethod is only shape-checked by the zod enum (line 393) and then passed verbatim into effectivePaymentMethod (line 611), the order doc (line 649), the payments/{orderId} doc (line 726) and the callable response (line 790); useWallet is similarly honoured with no walletEnabled check. The setting is live, not dead: written by admin/src/features/settings/routes/PaymentGatewayTab.tsx:41-48, typed in packages/shared/src/types/settings.ts:44-52, seeded in scripts/seed.ts:184 and scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:114, and enforced purely client-side in web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:158-174 and app/lib/features/checkout/checkout_screen.dart:317-345. No rules-level substitute exists because the order is written by the callable with admin credentials, so a stale client screen or a direct callable invocation can place a COD order that the admin disabled or that exceeds codMaxAmountPaise, decrementing stock and creating a payments row. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list and not on the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list; it also contradicts the project rule that money decisions are server-authoritative. One small correction to the claim's wording: settings/delivery.codSurchargePaise IS read for COD at line 349, but that is pricing, not the availability/limit gate, so the defect stands.

title: Approve confirmation and drawer hardcode "credited to the wallet" — the module never reads settings/returns.autoRefundToWallet
detail: The confirm dialog body (lines 218-226) states "{amount} will be credited to {customer}'s {refundTargetLabel(refundMethod)}" and, because requestReturnOrReplacement always writes refundMethod:'wallet' (functions/src/returns/requests.ts:133), refundTargetLabel() returns the hardcoded string 'Normal wallet' (api/returns.ts:50) for every pending request. The drawer repeats it unconditionally: "Approving credits this amount to the customer's wallet immediately and can't be undone." (lines 332-336), and the list 'To' column (line 178) shows 'Normal wallet' for every pending row. None of this is true when settings/returns.autoRefundToWallet is false — decisions.ts:107-108 then sets toWallet=false and rewrites refundMethod to 'gateway'. There is no import of the settings doc anywhere under admin/src/features/returns (the only reader/writer of autoRefundToWallet in admin is StorefrontTab.tsx:279-296), so the screen cannot know which mode it is in. The destination is also display-only: the module offers no control to pick wallet vs original method, even though the design prototype shows both ('Normal wallet' and 'Original' rows in designs/Barakath Admin Prototype.dc.html).
failure_scenario: Auto-refund is OFF. Admin opens #RP-000123, the drawer says 'Approving credits this amount to the customer's wallet immediately', the confirm says '₹899 will be credited to Aisha Khan's Normal wallet'. Admin clicks 'Approve & refund' believing the customer is paid, and sees the success toast 'Refund approved for #RP-000123'. Aisha's wallet balance is unchanged and no walletTransactions entry exists; the admin only discovers the discrepancy if the customer complains.
fix: Subscribe to settings/returns in the returns module; when autoRefundToWallet is false, change the destination label to 'Original payment method (manual payout)' and the confirm/drawer copy to 'This approves the return but does NOT move money — you must pay ₹X back manually.'

verdict.reason: Verified and could not refute the core. admin/src/features/returns/ contains only api/returns.ts and routes/ReturnsListPage.tsx, and neither reads settings/returns — the sole admin reader/writer of autoRefundToWallet is settings/routes/StorefrontTab.tsx (ReturnsCard, persisted toggle, defaults true). functions/src/returns/requests.ts:133 hardcodes refundMethod:'wallet' on every request, so refundTargetLabel() yields 'Normal wallet' for every pending row, while decisions.ts:28,107-108 sets toWallet=false and rewrites refundMethod to 'gateway' when the toggle is off — no wallet write, no walletTransactions doc, refundedAt null. The drawer text (ReturnsListPage.tsx:332-336) and confirm body (218-226) render before the call, so nothing server-side can correct them; and the CF explicitly returns {amount, creditedToWallet} (decisions.ts:182) which approveReturn() (api/returns.ts:60-63, typed Promise<void>) discards before doApprove fires an unconditional 'Refund approved' toast. Not on the already-fixed list (that entry covers the CF honouring autoRefundToWallet, which it does — the admin UI was never wired) and not known-intentional. Confidence is medium, not high, because the claim ignores real post-hoc mitigation: after approval the 'To'/Destination cell flips to 'Original' and the drawer timeline renders the CF's statusHistory note 'Approved — refund to be paid out manually (auto-refund to wallet is off).', so the discrepancy is discoverable without a customer complaint. Two sub-claims should be dropped: the 'mock-data' category is a mislabel (unconditional copy, not fixture data), and the missing wallet-vs-original picker is a design-parity wish, not a defect (destination is policy, not per-request). What remains is a genuine, cheaply fixable defect: pre-decision copy and the success toast assert money movement that does not occur when autoRefundToWallet is false.

title: Approving with auto-refund OFF tells the customer their money was refunded — app and order doc both claim a refund that never happened
detail: decisions.ts:157-167 increments order.refundedPaise by the full amount unconditionally, even in the manual-payout branch where no wallet credit and no gateway refund occurred (the Razorpay refund API is never called anywhere in functions/src). Downstream, app/lib/features/orders/data/order.dart:209 defines `wasRefunded => refundedPaise > 0 || paymentStatus == 'refunded'`, and the app's return card at app/lib/features/orders/order_detail_screen.dart:529-531 branches purely on request status: `if (r.isApproved) _refundLine('$refund refunded to your wallet', brandGreen, check_circle)`. ReturnRequest.isApproved is `status == 'approved' || status == 'completed'` (return_request.dart:36) — it never looks at refundedAt or refundMethod. So the moment the admin approves, the customer app shows a green tick and the words '₹899 refunded to your wallet' even though the wallet was untouched, and the admin reports screen counts the order as refunded (admin/src/features/reports/api/reports.ts:233,248).
failure_scenario: Auto-refund is OFF. Admin approves the return. The customer opens the order in the app, sees '₹899 refunded to your wallet' with a green check, opens the Wallet screen and finds the balance unchanged and no refund entry in the ledger — a direct contradiction between two screens of the same app, triggered by an admin click.
fix: Only increment order.refundedPaise (and only claim a refund to the customer) when money actually moved; in the manual branch write a distinct marker (e.g. refundPendingPaise / statusHistory-driven copy) and make the app's refund line read refundedAt/refundMethod so it says 'Approved — refund will be paid to your original payment method' until settlement.

verdict.reason: Confirmed reachable and real. With settings/returns.autoRefundToWallet=false (a live admin toggle written by admin/src/features/settings/routes/StorefrontTab.tsx:296,329), functions/src/returns/decisions.ts:107-108,139 approves the return with toWallet=false, refundedAt=null, refundMethod='gateway', no walletTransactions entry, and no gateway refund (no Razorpay refund API exists in functions/src). The app then asserts the opposite: app/lib/features/orders/order_detail_screen.dart:529-531 renders a green check plus '<amount> refunded to your wallet' branching only on ReturnRequest.isApproved (return_request.dart:36 = status approved|completed), and :568 hardcodes the timeline label 'Approved · refund issued'. The model parses refundMethod (return_request.dart:30,59) but grep shows no screen reads it, and refundedAt is not parsed at all — so the data needed to render truthfully is present and ignored. The customer sees 'refunded to your wallet' on the order screen and an unchanged balance/empty ledger on the Wallet screen, triggered by one admin click. Not covered by the already-fixed item ('autoRefundToWallet is honoured' — the CF does honour it; the app does not) nor by the intentional list. Two sub-claims are overstated but do not rescue it: (a) the CF's statusHistory note 'Approved — refund to be paid out manually' IS rendered in small secondary text below the green line (order_detail_screen.dart:610), so the card self-contradicts rather than being silently wrong; (b) order.refundedPaise -> Order.wasRefunded (order.dart:209) only surfaces at orders_screen.dart:288 inside an `status == cancelled` branch, unreachable for returns, and admin reports.ts:248 would flag the order as refunded anyway via refundedOrderIds() (reports.ts:232) regardless of the increment — so the decisions.ts:158 increment itself is defensible as the documented over-refund guard. The genuine, fixable defect is the app's unconditional 'refunded to your wallet' copy (and 'refund issued' timeline label) on an approval that moved no money.

title: PaymentsListPage swallows the Firestore listener error and renders the empty state instead
detail: `useLiveCollection` surfaces `{data, loading, error}` (hooks/firestoreCache.ts:117-121 sets `error` on the snapshot error callback) but line 22 destructures only `{ data: payments, loading }` and the render (lines 100-103) has no error branch: on error `loading` becomes false and `payments` stays `[]`, so the table falls through to `payments.length === 0 ? 'No payments yet.'`. Other screens in the app (DeliveryTaxTab.tsx:118, PaymentGatewayTab.tsx:69) do render an error card, so this is an omission, not a house style.
failure_scenario: A sub-admin whose custom claims haven't propagated, or any rules/index failure on the `payments` orderBy query, opens /payments and is told "No payments yet." — an authoritative-looking statement that the store has taken zero money. Nothing is logged to the user and the header confidently prints "₹0 this month · 0 failed".
fix: Destructure `error` and render a "Couldn't load payments. Please refresh." card, matching the settings tabs.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in code: /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/payments/routes/PaymentsListPage.tsx:22 destructures only {data, loading} from usePaymentsList(), and the file contains zero references to `error` (grep -c error = 0), so the tbody at lines 100-103 renders 'No payments yet.' and the header at line 78 renders '₹0 this month · 0 failed' when the listener fails. useLiveCollection does surface the error (hooks/firestoreCache.ts:117-121 sets {data: prev ?? [], loading:false, error}). This is an omission, not house style: CouponsListPage:124, NotificationsListPage:74, SpinnerListPage:89, BannerListPage:77, SubAdminListPage:30, ReturnsListPage, ReviewsListPage and ProductsListPage all read and render `error`; only Payments and OrdersListPage:26 do not. No global error boundary or snapshot-error toast catches it. I did partially refute the reporter's stated trigger: a sub-admin with unpropagated claims can never reach /payments, because initAuthListener→loadAdminDoc reads admins/{uid}, which firestore.rules:196-198 gates on the role claim, so such a user is bounced to /login; and the 'missing index' trigger is implausible since orderBy('createdAt','desc') is a single-field auto-indexed query and firestore.indexes.json has "fieldOverrides": []. But the defect survives via reachable paths: payments read requires isAdmin() (rules:83), so a session whose role claim is revoked or admin suspended mid-session (token refreshes hourly) that then opens Payments for the first time gets a cold-start permission-denied, as does any resource-exhausted/quota error — both render the authoritative-looking 'No payments yet.' plus ₹0 revenue on the one screen where a false zero matters most. Real, fixable, one-line-plus-error-row change mirroring CouponsListPage. Medium confidence only because the trigger is narrow and the severity is UI-state rather than data corruption.

title: Return refunds never settle the payments/{orderId} document, unlike the cancellation path
detail: The approve transaction updates orderRequests, the order (refundedPaise, paymentStatus, embedded items), the customer wallet, the product soldCount and commissions — but never touches payments/{orderId}. functions/src/orders/cancel.ts:79-80,219-223 does exactly the opposite: it reads payments/{orderId} up front and settles it to status 'refunded' precisely so "the admin Payments page doesn't keep showing a captured/pending payment". The admin Payments list renders that document's status directly (admin/src/features/payments/api/payments.ts:9-29, PaymentsListPage.tsx:106). Additionally, decisions.ts:159-162 flips order.paymentStatus to 'refunded' only when the refund is full AND wallet-mode, and 'partial_refund' is never written by any Cloud Function (grep: it exists only in packages/shared/src/enums.ts:70 and in the two admin pill mappers, payments.ts:25 and orders/api/orders.ts:73), so the entire partial-refund pill is dead code.
failure_scenario: Admin approves a ₹899 return on a fully captured ₹899 online order. Orders list now shows the order as 'Refunded'; the Payments list still shows that transaction as 'Success/Captured' with the full amount and no refund trace, so the two Operations screens disagree and the payments export used for reconciliation overstates net collections. For a partial return (one item of three) neither screen shows anything at all.
fix: Read payments/{orderId} inside the approve transaction and update it to 'refunded' or 'partial_refund' based on refundedPaise vs amountPaise, mirroring cancel.ts:219-223.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. functions/src/returns/decisions.ts:157 updates the order (refundedPaise, paymentStatus, items), wallet, soldCount and commissions but never touches payments/{orderId}; grep shows the only writers of that doc are checkout.ts (placeOrder/markPaymentFailed/verifyPayment) and cancel.ts:219-223, which settles it to 'refunded' specifically so the admin Payments page stops showing a captured payment. There are no Firestore triggers in the repo (zero onDocumentWritten/Updated/Created hits) and no client writer (only firestore.rules:91 and the read-only usePaymentsList), so nothing reconciles it later. Impact is functional, not cosmetic: PaymentsListPage.tsx:29-41 sums amountPaise for status==='captured' into the "this month" KPI and onExport(true) filters the GST-invoice CSV on 'captured', so a fully wallet-refunded return stays in both while the Orders list shows the order as Refunded. The partial_refund sub-claim also holds — occurrences are only packages/shared/src/enums.ts:70, admin payments.ts:25, orders/api/orders.ts:73 and reports.ts:226 (all consumers); seed.ts never writes it. Partial mitigation exists but only in Reports: reports.ts:242-249 derives isRefunded from refundedPaise/orderRequests as well, so the refund-rate KPI is fine; the Payments module has no such fallback. Not on the already-fixed list (which names placeOrder/verifyPayment/cancel and pointedly omits returns) nor the intentional list. Minor nuance: with autoRefundToWallet OFF the order also stays 'captured', so the divergence is specific to the default wallet-auto-refund path.

title: Opening Refunds streams the entire customers collection live, purely to map uid → name
detail: ReturnsListPage calls useCustomersList(), which attaches an unbounded real-time listener to `query(collection(db,'customers'), orderBy('createdAt','desc'))` (admin/src/features/customers/api/customers.ts:10-13) with no limit, solely to build nameByUid (line 47) for the 10 rows on screen. orderRequests itself is also fetched whole with no limit (api/returns.ts:25-27) — defensible per its documented rationale, but it grows without bound and every admin session re-downloads all history. Unlike orders, which denormalise customerName onto the doc (used by OrdersListPage), orderRequests carries no customer name, forcing this join. The customers listener's error state is also discarded (only `data` is destructured), so a failed/denied customers read silently degrades every row and the CSV export to raw uids with no warning.
failure_scenario: On a store with 40k customers, an admin clicking 'Refunds' to review one pending return downloads and keeps live 40k customer documents; the page takes seconds to become useful and Firestore bills 40k reads per visit. If that read fails, the table and barkath-refunds.csv show 28-character uids in the Customer column with no error shown, and the search box stops matching customer names.
fix: Denormalise customerName (and customerPhone) onto the orderRequests doc in requestReturnOrReplacement the way orders already do, and drop the useCustomersList() join; failing that, fetch only the uids on the current page and surface the customers-read error.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. ReturnsListPage.tsx:38 attaches the unbounded live customers query (admin/src/features/customers/api/customers.ts:10-13, no limit) solely to build nameByUid (line 47) for the 10 visible rows, the search filter, the CSV and the drawer text. There is no global prefetch of CUSTOMERS_KEY, and firestoreCache.ts tears the listener down at zero refs while lib/firebase.ts initialises Firestore with the default memory cache (no persistentLocalCache), so each visit to Refunds re-downloads the whole collection. This is an outlier, not the house pattern: Order.customerName and Review.customerName (packages/shared/src/types/commerce.ts:138,192) and WithdrawalRequest.customerName are denormalised, so Orders/Reviews/Affiliate lists do no join; only OrderRequest (commerce.ts:160-186) omits it, forcing this one join. The fix is cheap and server-side: functions/src/returns/requests.ts already holds the order doc inside its transaction (it reads o.shortId, o.subtotalPaise, o.discountPaise) and could write customerName at creation, with the uid fallback kept for old docs. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Caveat: the secondary error-swallow point is weak — firestore.rules:157 lets any admin read customers, so there is no sub-admin permission-denied path and the failure degrades gracefully to uids; the perf severity also scales with customer count and is invisible on seed data.
